topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This section introduces the lecture's aims and frames the concepts of cancer evolution, cell of origin, and the tumor microenvironment.

topics.label: Clonal selection and Darwinian evolution driven by somatic mutations
topics.groupedBecause: This section presents experimental evidence that tumors develop through the stepwise acquisition of mutations conferring competitive growth advantages to cellular clones.

topics.label: Epigenetic regulation and transcriptional changes in tumor development
topics.groupedBecause: This section demonstrates how non-mutational, transient disruptions in chromatin regulation can drive oncogenic transformation.

topics.label: Cell of origin and stem cell hierarchies in cancer initiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the role of tissue stem cells, progenitor hierarchies, and cellular plasticity in tumor initiation using leukemia and intestinal crypt models.

topics.label: Environmental promoters and inflammatory signaling in tumor outgrowth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate how environmental promoters and chronic inflammatory signals cooperate with pre-existing mutations to enable malignant outgrowth.

topics.label: Stromal dependence of established tumors and therapeutic targeting
topics.groupedBecause: This section examines the requirement of stromal and supportive cells for maintaining established tumors and discusses microenvironment-targeted therapies.

topics.label: Methodological tools for studying tumor evolution and microenvironment
topics.groupedBecause: This section reviews single-cell sequencing, spatial omics, and computational methods used to investigate tumor evolution and cellular interactions.

topics.label: Synthesis of evolutionary and microenvironmental drivers of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics provide an integrative summary of cancer evolution as an interplay between mutations, cell state, and microenvironment, and conclude the lecture.
